label: implicitly sets parameter
type: the subject surface (a shell, a UI, a request mode) supplies the object parameter on the user's behalf, so the user does not pass it explicitly. The inverse of requiresSetting.
note: 14 occurrences over 6 files, all in the SQL++ transaction family. Load-bearing because it is exactly what differs between surfaces: cbq and the Query Workbench set txid for you; a multi-statement REST request does not, so the same documented statement sequence behaves differently depending on where it is typed. Answers a competency question the registry previously could not: 'which of these parameters do I actually have to pass?'
